name: call_exec_alloc_entry
description: Calls the exec library's AllocEntry function through a library base held in a global variable, leaving the result for the caller.

name: start_cli_session
description: Starts a command-line interpreter session by opening a new console window and running the CLI and Shell startup scripts named in its text. A control block is allocated and freed only when called with zero, and the result is that of the last library call.

name: build_node_chain_from_list
description: Walks a list of value records, allocating an eight-byte node for each one, storing the record's value in it and linking the nodes in order. It stops when an allocation fails or a value is zero, and returns the first node.

name: free_node_chain
description: Walks a linked list of nodes, releasing each node's payload and then the eight-byte node itself, until the list ends at a zero link.

name: parse_signed_decimal
description: Reads a signed decimal integer from a null-terminated string, accepting an optional leading plus or minus sign and stopping at the first non-digit. It returns the value with the sign applied.

name: call_library_entry_198
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function 198 bytes below that base, passing on the caller's arguments. The library function is not identified by this code.

name: divide_32bit_with_remainder
description: Divides one 32-bit unsigned value by another and returns the quotient and remainder as a pair. Large divisors use a bit-by-bit shift-and-subtract loop, while divisors that fit in 16 bits use two 16-bit divide steps.

name: multiply_32bit_integers
description: Multiplies two 32-bit values using four 16-bit partial products and keeps the low 32 bits of the product. It also returns the second input with its two halves swapped.

name: negate_result_on_flag
description: Calls a routine and returns its first result, negated when its second result is non-zero.

name: scan_disk_bitmap_flags
description: Main routine of the Disk-Validator program. It clears a run of 32-bit flag words, tests single bits of table words against bit masks, and writes a one-digit count into a text buffer. The listing is truncated before its end, so the later steps are not known.

name: copy_memory_then_call_target
description: Program entry that copies a block of memory through the exec library's copy routine, reached via a library base in a global variable, then makes a second indirect call. That call's target is not resolved in this listing.

name: release_blit_state_slot
description: Runs a fixed sequence of library calls, including a memory free, repeated over three passes. It then reads a stored word for the current entry and, if it holds one particular pattern, saves it to a global and clears the slot. It returns its two input registers unchanged.

name: decrement_until_minus_one
description: Decrements a 16-bit counter register until it reaches minus one, then returns. It has no other effect.

name: decode_bitstream_passes
description: Runs seven passes of a bit-stream decoder that reads variable-length codes and uses them to copy or add values within a buffer. Afterwards it calls the exec cache-clear routine when a size field exceeds a threshold.

name: enter_bitstream_decoder_loop
description: Two-instruction entry point, called by the reschedule stub, that merges zero into a data register. Its decompiled body is the bit-stream decoder loop, which the listing records as only two instructions, so the exact entry is unclear and the body is truncated.

name: decode_bitstream_byte_loop
description: Bit-stream decoder working on byte-sized values: it reads variable-length codes from the input and copies or adds values within the output buffer in a loop. It is called by the reschedule stub, and the listing is truncated before its end.

name: copy_decoded_runs_to_output
description: Copies decoded bytes into an output buffer four at a time, taking run lengths from the same bit stream as the decoder, and stops when a counter reaches zero. It returns the first four bytes it wrote.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The entry of a keymap data file that the decompiler decodes as instructions. The code is only bad instruction data, so no routine is recovered here.

name: release_state_slot_after_calls
